post_title: What will the October 2026 US PPI for final demand (seasonally adjusted, month-over-month) be as first published by BLS?

question.title: What will the October 2026 US PPI for final demand (seasonally adjusted, month-over-month) be as first published by BLS?
question.description:
US producer price inflation has accelerated sharply in 2026. The PPI for final demand rose 1.3% month-over-month (seasonally adjusted) in September 2026 — the largest monthly gain since March 2022 and more than double the roughly 0.6% consensus — after 0.5% in August (upwardly revised from 0.4%), 0.2% in July and -0.1% in June; the 12-month rate jumped to 6.3%, the highest since December 2022. Energy did nearly all of the work in September: final demand energy +10.8%, gasoline +20.3%, crude petroleum +28.3%, while final demand less foods, energy and trade services rose 0.5% ([September 2026 release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_10152026.htm)).

The driver is the US war with Iran, which has restricted global energy supply. Brent crude has risen roughly 16.6% over the past month to about $114/bbl (October 29) and WTI to about $103, even as US retail gasoline eased to about $4.25/gal on the switch to cheaper winter-blend fuel (AAA, October 28). Monthly PPI prints have been unusually hard to predict — the September consensus missed by more than half a point — and renewed US strikes on Iran after the November 3 midterms have been under discussion, so the October energy contribution is genuinely uncertain.

The Fed, which hiked in September, left its target range at 3.75%–4.00% at its October 27–28 meeting; the October PPI print is one of the last major inflation readings before the December 8–9 FOMC. BLS publishes the October 2026 PPI on Friday, November 13, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET ([BLS November 2026 schedule](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/2026/11_sched.htm)); the November PPI is not released until December 15. October CPI is published earlier, on November 10, so forecasters will have a partial read on October energy and food prices when this question opens.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves on the value of the seasonally adjusted 1-month percent change in the Producer Price Index for final demand for October 2026, as first published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) in its Producer Price Index news release at 8:30 a.m. ET on November 13, 2026 ([release page](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ppi.nr0.htm)). The resolved value is that published percent figure from the release's opening statement and Table A — e.g., if BLS reports that final demand prices "increased 0.7 percent in October, seasonally adjusted," the question resolves as 0.7. Later revisions to the October 2026 figure do not change the resolution. If the October 2026 figure is absent from that release but BLS publishes it in a later release, the question resolves on that first published value; if BLS never publishes an October 2026 final demand PPI month-over-month change, the question is annulled.
question.fine_print: Only the total "final demand" index counts — not final demand goods, not "final demand less foods, energy, and trade services," not the 12-month (year-over-year) change, and not the unadjusted change. If the BLS release page is unavailable after publication, the same BLS figure as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) may be used.
